a.text: 'As the wind combs through golden wheat,'
'The forest wild wi' pipes of steel clank and beat,'
'I found by the edge of a plate my dear love true, and following a firelight straight from the blue...'

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: So that's how the second half of the song goes...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: How sad.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Now Damian's gone, and he won't even get a decent burial...

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: They'd never give him back to us. All they'd do is scorch him to ash, scatter him off the city, treat him like the dirt under anyone's foot.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: (Soft sobbing)

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: First it was Lowry, then it was Chris, and now they've caught hold of Damian too. Grainne, when Sean got arrested, they all said he'd caught Oripathy—

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: No, Ronan, don't go on. Sean... he just caught it being careless.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: He was a hardworking, loyal man. A poor, poor man, and the only thing he ever wanted was just a better life for me and my son...

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: Grainne, haven't you figured it out?

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: We're just a bunch of rivets to them. Of course they'll toss us away without a care when we rust.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: And even if we haven't rusted, so long as we don't fit too well in the city's machines, we've got the same fate coming. Nothing changes.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: They never gave a shit we were catching Oripathy one by one.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: Every month they give out those drugs, the other workers get their whole lot, and we can only expect a half. Maybe even a third.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: And the protective suits. How long has Sean been wearing his for? Five years? Bloody hell, seven? How many times have you snuck out of bed at night just to patch it up?

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: All those laws, all those standards, just for their benefit. And us?

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: We're only fit to eat the potatoes and the rotten apples they don't want. Means nothing that the ag plates of this city soak in our sweat.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: We're only fit to waste away our lives day and night in the factories, and once we can't work a day more, we fall ill one by one just like they wanted!

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: The way this is going, it's like they're sitting there playing dominoes, wiping us Tarans off our own city—

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Stop it... I'm begging you. Ronan, nothing you're saying will lead to any good.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Just look at Cliodhna and her kin stood over there. Crying over their own son, their own brother. How many more loves do you want lost, how many more hurting over what your anger did for them?

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: It's the murderers that brought this hurt. They're killing us one after another. Times it's with sickness, times it's with mortar shells. Grainne, don't you deceive yourself any longer.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: (Low voice) This morning, a few came looking for me. The O'Briens, and Conor's brother. They've decided to join us.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: It's been hard getting by for you and your kid, we understand. This is a big moment, and we need to help each other now more than ever...

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: You'd better keep far from me and my child, Ronan... seeing as my Sean got on well enough with your lot.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: I have to go, Grainne. You see that one over there? She's wearing that uniform.

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: You know our rules. I trust in you, and I'm asking you to trust me more. If you've made up your mind, you can tell Saoirse.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Hello!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Er... hello.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Do you know Barry's, er, Damian Barry's family?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I heard you singin' just now. I'm not in the wrong place.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: I... I don't know what you're searching about for, but Damian's ma and sister know nothing.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Then did he have any especially good friends, or anyone who worked at the warehouse with him?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: We know nothing... That's the truth...

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: *Whimper*... I'm begging you! Please don't take me...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Huh? Sorry... did I get too close? I've got no intentions of hurtin' you.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You seem awful scared of me. Is somethin' on my face?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: N... Nothing at all...

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: If you'll allow me, I need to go home. I still have so much fruit from this morning, and it'll go rotten in no time, if I leave it alone...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: *Sigh*.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh? Is that... Captain Kelly?

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Cliodhna, I just want to see you for one moment. I want to know if you and Fiona are still alright...

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Yes, it was my mistake, but—

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: My hands were tied...

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Of course I remember, I remember it all. Damian... he was the boy of my sister.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: I watched him grow up his whole life. The day I was transferred back from Peninsula to Hillock, he set an edelweiss in my cap with his own two hands.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: He was still so little then... I...

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: I'm sorry... I shouldn't be telling you all this.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: You're right... I've been good for nothing. I haven't the face to return here.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: I wasn't in time to stop him when he got involved with that group... and I couldn't disobey the Colonel's orders.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Not just that, I have to do this. This is all for County Hillock.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: I love you all, and I love this city... I can't just stand goggling while that bunch tear our home to pieces.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: I understand, Cliodhna, my sister, and I'm not asking your forgiveness or anything.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: I'll... be going, then. You... you and Fiona be sure to take care of yourselves.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: If I can find the time tomorrow, I'll come see you again...

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: *Cough*, *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: What are you—

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Oh, just... just a boy.

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Are you... *cough* *cough*—are you hurt? Don't run too fast now. It's been decades, and they've still never levelled the road here...

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Traitor!

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Wh—What did you say?

steps.name: Craig
steps.text: Traitor!!!

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Craig! What are you doing?! Get back here now!

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: And what's that ball in your hands for... oh, forget it, you're always gripping that ball wherever you go. Were you off looking for Conor's brother again? Oh, you... Ronan's told you, hasn't he?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Look at your hands, all covered in black. It's like you were digging through a mine.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: You come with me to the morning market from now on. You can't go looking for them around this time anymore... I can't let you become like them...

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Traitor?

steps.name: Captain Kelly
steps.text: Boy... wasn't one bit wrong.
The Captain stands still for a moment, repeating the word, once, twice to himself, finally turning to leave.
His head is hung low as could be, and he doesn't meet the gaze of a single person more, including those young colleagues of him that rush his way.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Hold on a moment, Captain...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You—What are you all doing here? Pack off home, if you know what's good for you!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: We've told you, you're not allowed to congregate on the streets at this time!

steps.name: Embittered Man
steps.text: This is our home! It's not us who should go packing!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: —Who had the lip to say that just now?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: What are these... Wilted leaves?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Step forward right now!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You Tara rabble, watch I don't—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Brandishin' a bolt on the street's far too dangerous!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Who're you?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ah, I'm here on orders. Come to investigate the case.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You're here for the murder at the bar?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Er, what murder?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: This rabble right here. They've killed plenty of ours.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: ...Damian Barry?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Right, I hear he's been put to death already. I suppose it was you lot who caught him? Nicely done, thank you.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: We didn't know yet when we caught him... was he really part of the spectre force? Er...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Who gives a shake what he was? Serves him right he's dead!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Did you hear me? No—congregating! Each and all of you up to whatever secret business here, you'll all be treated as suspects!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You bloody Tara arselickers—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Don't! Don't get carried away! Look, most of 'em are just plain city folk, with a loved one dead, and they're here grievin' for him, like human nature would.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Uh—a—a rotten potato?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Ha ha, see? You spoke for them, and you got battered, right?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: If you're so keen on staying here, stay. As long as I make sure this rabble behaves itself, I'm done. My rotten luck for getting this patrol duty.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You riff-raff, I'll say it again, no congregating!!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, it's just more and more rottin' leaves...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Come this way.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh, what?
'Reporting in, 9th Defence attacked...'
'Reporting in, 13th Defence currently in firefight...'

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Send notice one more time, please. I want to see Colonel Hamilton.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: The Colonel's handling urgent affairs.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You said that two hours ago.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I've already abided by strict process. I submitted description of my duty yesterday when entering County Hillock.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If the Colonel won't let us take part in suspect interrogations, and goes to lengths to execute them beforehand, and presently refuses my request to meet him—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: To anyone else, don't you think this conduct might be taken as a deliberate hindrance to our fulfillment of orders?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: I have no authority to answer your question, Lieutenant.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: That's fine. I'll say my part, and it's enough if someone listens.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I've said before, the Originium products thieved are not small in number. It's sufficient arms to allow a detachment to attack a small town, or bomb a medium nomadic city's support tracks.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Who'd want to obtain these products?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Ordinary bandits wouldn't need them; it'd cost too much to smuggle them out. With Victorian military goods in this great a bulk, even a Sargon black market under Columbia's protection wouldn't dare provide a means for a deal.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Who else is left? A local private arms dealer, moneymaking off the costs of remodeling? They haven't got the appetite, let alone the guts.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Only a well-trained unit, well-versed in military methods would dare take it, and could evade our spies on top.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If this unit got hold of that large a quantity of Originium product, what would their goal be?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Conspiracy to overthrow? Taking the chance to embezzle far removed from Londinium, colluding with outside powers to fill their pockets, slowly and steadily?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Lieutenant...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: No need to panic, this is all just baseless reasoning, no thanks to whoever's keeping me waiting. I can't get anything done like this.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: (Subdued communications)

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Lieutenant, the Colonel says he'll be here imminently.
